problems: The phenotype claims should distinguish lack of causal evidence from lack of any variant-specific disease association: E24c reports a prognosis difference for C250T in glioblastoma, while E24d suggests reduced involvement in telomere-related mechanisms.

TERT is a strong positional candidate because the variant lies in its promoter, but the available evidence does not directly demonstrate an effect of the cCRE on TERT expression; E06 has no TERT eQTL or CRISPR link.

The binding predictions are in-vitro computational predictions. Even the matched U-87MG E2F1 peak in E22 does not establish allele-specific occupancy or show that E2F1 mediates the predicted allelic effect.

Here we used pooled CRISPR/Cas9-based approaches to identify vulnerabilities associated with telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations (TPMs) found in >80% of glioblastomas.
Further, we found that TPMs are associated with expression of gene programs regulated by a wide array of ETS-factors in both cell lines and primary glioblastoma tissues.
In our series, patients exhibiting the C250T mutation had a more favorable prognosis compared to those with either TERPp-wt or TERTp C228T mutations.
Additionally, our findings suggest a reduced involvement of the C250T mutation in the underlying biological mechanisms related to telomeres.
